issue.title: Recordings linkage + restore chapter_assignment FK/index via migration
issue.body:
### Current state on main

Good `recordings` table (keep as-is) (`src/db/schema.ts:80`): `id TEXT PK`, `bible_text_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES bible_texts(id)`, `local_file_path`, `blob_key`, `duration_ms`, `file_size_bytes`, `take_number`, `is_latest`, `sync_status DEFAULT 'pending'`, `upload_error`, timestamps; indexes `idx_rec_verse`, `idx_rec_pending`.

Regressions in `chapter_assignments` (`src/db/schema.ts:50`):

```sql
assigned_user_id INTEGER , -- lost: REFERENCES users(id)
...
status TEXT NOT NULL, -- lost: DEFAULT
```

- The `idx_ca_assigned_user` index is **absent** (only `idx_ca_project_unit` exists, `:66`). `getMyWorkChapters` filters `WHERE ca.assigned_user_id = ?` (`queries.ts:335`) with no supporting index.
- Migrations are an **ad-hoc array** `chapterAssignmentMigrations` (`schema.ts:108`), run blindly in `db/index.ts:68` — not a versioned framework (#110).
- Recordings have **no `chapter_assignment_id` and no user column**; `queries.ts` wrongly joins on `r.chapter_assignment_id` (fixed in #98).

### Problems / why

- Dropped FK on `assigned_user_id` removes referential integrity for the core "my work" relationship.
- Missing `idx_ca_assigned_user` makes the My Work query do a full scan.
- `status` losing its default means inserts that omit status will fail/insert nulls inconsistently (repository currently always passes a value, but the constraint should be defensive).
- The upload worker (#100) needs a reliable way to attribute a recording to a verse (and, via #105, a user); the current schema/query mismatch blocks correct aggregates.

### Target design

Express all changes as **versioned migration steps** (#110), not edits to `createTableQueries` (existing devices already have these tables):

```sql
-- restore integrity on chapter_assignments (via migration; SQLite needs table rebuild for FK/default)
-- 1) create chapter_assignments_new with:
-- assigned_user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id)
-- status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'not_started'
-- 2) copy data, drop old, rename
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ca_assigned_user ON chapter_assignments(assigned_user_id);
```

- Recordings linkage: confirm verse-based linkage (`bible_text_id`) is sufficient for upload attribution; if a direct assignment reference is needed, add a nullable `chapter_assignment_id INTEGER REFERENCES chapter_assignments(id)` via migration. Prefer keeping `bible_text_id` as the canonical link (matches #98).
- User attribution column is owned by #105 (D3) — coordinate, do not duplicate.

### Coordination note (avoid duplication)

- **#103 (D1)** owns the `chapter_assignments` / `user_projects` FK + index restoration migration. This ticket (#99) owns **recordings linkage** and references #103 for the `assigned_user_id` FK so the rebuild happens **once** in the F2 (#110) migration set.
- **#110 (F2)** must land first to provide `user_version`-based migrations.
- **#105 (D3)** owns any user-attribution column on recordings.

### Implementation steps

1. Depend on #110 migration framework.
2. Add migration(s) to restore `assigned_user_id REFERENCES users(id)`, `status ... DEFAULT 'not_started'`, and `idx_ca_assigned_user` (implemented jointly with #103 — single migration).
3. Decide & document recordings linkage (keep `bible_text_id`; optionally add nullable `chapter_assignment_id`).
4. Update `repository.ts` insert (`insertChapterAssignmentTx`) to rely on the restored default where appropriate.
5. Verify `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` (already set in `db/index.ts:62`) does not break existing inserts (order of table rebuild matters).
6. Tests: migration brings an old-shape DB to the new shape; FK violation rejected; `idx_ca_assigned_user` present.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `chapter_assignments.assigned_user_id` references `users(id)` again; `status` has `DEFAULT 'not_started'`; `idx_ca_assigned_user` exists — all via the #110 framework.
- [ ] No destructive rewrite of `createTableQueries` that would wipe existing device data.
- [ ] Recordings↔verse linkage documented and consistent with #98 (no `chapter_assignment_id` join unless a real column is added).
- [ ] Migration tested from an old-shape DB; FK enforcement verified.

### Test plan / verification

```bash
npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --ci
```

- Tests default `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:9999` via `jest.env.cjs`; **no live API required** — runs against local SQLite/mocked DB.
- Do **not** use `FLUENT_USER_EMAIL`.

### Out of scope

- Migration framework itself (#110), user-attribution column (#105), upload worker (#100), multi-take repo logic (#98).

### Links

- Epic: #117
- Related: #110 (F2 migrations), #103 (D1 — joint FK migration), #105 (D3 attribution), #98 (recordings join fix)
- Anti-pattern: [PR #82](https://github.com/eten-tech-foundation/fluent-mobile/pull/82) `schema.ts` destructive rewrite — do not copy.

comments.body: Related: #121 — the three `recordings` joins in `src/db/queries.ts` reference a non-existent `chapter_assignment_id` column. The linkage decision in this ticket (add column vs join through `bible_texts`) determines the fix for #121.
